claims.text: The proposed material is a powder-metallurgically produced AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 high-entropy alloy.
A short dwell at approximately 800–900 °C in a controlled oxidizing environment can form a stable oxide-based barrier on AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
A dwell of several minutes in a tailored environment promotes formation of a spinel-type oxide on AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
The surface treatment produces an in-situ oxide/spinel layer on AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
A durable oxide barrier can reduce chemical attack by hindering interfacial reactions and further oxidation.
The oxide/spinel barrier reduces mechanical wear damage under tribo-corrosive contact.
Oxide-treated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 should have significantly better elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion resistance than conventional structural alloys.
Oxide-treated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 should exhibit a significantly lower combined tribo-corrosion rate than conventional alloys under identical conditions.
The reduction in material loss could be multiple-fold.
Conventional high-temperature structural alloys lacking effective protective oxide layers experience accelerated oxidation.
Conventional high-temperature structural alloys lacking protective spinel layers experience accelerated mechanical wear.
The proposed performance has been demonstrated at moderate to high temperatures up to approximately 900 °C.
Performance in more aggressive chemical media or above approximately 900 °C remains unverified.
Direct tribo-corrosion data for oxide-engineered AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 are limited.
The long-term stability of spinel layers under continuously changing environments is not fully established.
